lead: The Egoscue method is a set of personalised stretches and floor exercises developed by Pete Egoscue to restore alignment.
People use it to stand straighter and move with less pain, available through clinics and his books.

paras: Exercises target specific muscles believed to hold the pelvis and spine out of alignment, with the goal of resetting posture.
The exercises are low-impact. Success figures come from the publisher; clinical studies are not available. Persistent pain warrants medical assessment.

angle.text: Followers use the exercises to correct slouching and uneven alignment, aiming for a straighter, taller-looking posture along with less pain.

lead: The Egoscue method is a postural therapy created by Pete Egoscue, built around personalised stretches and exercises, often called e-cises, meant to restore body alignment. People use it to improve posture and reduce musculoskeletal discomfort, with a more upright, balanced stance as the visible result [1][2].

The publisher of his book describes Egoscue as a wounded Marine officer in Vietnam who became a physical therapist and built clinics around the approach, and states that the method avoids drugs, surgery and manipulation [1]. The books Pain Free and The Egoscue Method of Health Through Motion present it to general readers. The 95 percent success rate cited by the publisher is a self-reported figure.

paras: Sessions assign individual sets of gentle stretches and strengthening moves for specific muscles, with the stated aim of restoring alignment [1]. A frequently mentioned exercise is lying on the floor with the legs at 90 degrees and the calves on a chair, often called the static back position [3].

sections.h: Use in looksmaxxing and lifting communities
paras: Strength-training forums mention the books as a source for back pain and posture work, and some lifters report using the exercises in their warm-ups and recovery [4][5][6]. One poster describes trying them for pelvic alignment along with shoulder mobilisations [7].

lore.intro: On T Nation, the method is recommended in threads about back pain and posture as an alternative or complement to gym work [3][4][6].
